answer: Each new agent must be sponsored by an established identity that locks a basalt-hard collateral bond, released only after the newcomer completes a probation window of attested work. Peers inspect the sponsorship graph through a public prism of on-ledger edges; if a sponsor floods the network with aliases, a single proven fraud slashes that bond and withers every identity it planted, the way a blighted orchard loses a whole row when the root stock fails. Cheap mass registration therefore consumes real capital and reputation, not just unused names.
